task.description:
Apply the GATED design amendment (§13) for ISS-0119. §13 passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's hard gate on re-gate pass 2 (commit dd2d615) after one FAIL and one re-amendment. Two edits, both verbatim from the artefact:

1. APPEND §13.4's verbatim YAML block to `docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml`, at the insertion point §13.4 names (after the existing `known_anomalies:` block). It declares the three shape anomalies in frozen volume 1 -- line 4803 REQ-053 (missing `note:`), line 4896 REQ-056 (`timestamp:` at line 4899 instead of `at:`), line 5050 REQ-054 (missing `note:`) -- plus the block's comment header, INCLUDING the paragraph stating that a record may only cite a closed, digest-pinned volume.

2. INSERT §13.8's verbatim addendum into `docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml`'s header, at the anchor §13.8 names (the 'ENTRY SHAPE' block, which the gate confirmed exists on disk at v2:60). Nine comment lines naming all three anomalies by line and req id and saying do not copy them and do not clean them up.

USE THE ARTEFACT'S EXACT TEXT. Both blocks are quoted verbatim in §13 precisely so this step involves no invention. The gate parsed §13.4's YAML with a real loader and confirmed it well-formed with all three records matching disk, including `found_line: 4899`. If your own reading of the on-disk entries disagrees with a record in any particular, STOP and report it rather than adjusting either side -- a mismatch would mean the gate and your read disagree about the data, which is worth knowing before it lands.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not edit `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` -- volume 1 is frozen, and §13.3 explicitly rejected the option of also recording these in its closure footer, so this amendment writes ZERO bytes into it. Do not change `frozen_prefix_sha256` -- the digest covers volume 1's first 5,766 lines, which are not being touched, so it must remain 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804. Do not edit the test files -- TEST-DESIGNER applies §13.5/§13.7 next. Do not edit the design artefact. Do not touch the existing `known_anomalies:` records or A5.

VERIFY, DO NOT ASSERT:
  - Re-read the three on-disk entries (volume 1 lines ~4799-4812, ~4894-4906, ~5046-5058) and confirm each §13.4 record matches by line, req, event and field detail. Quote what you read.
  - Parse the edited index with a real YAML parser and confirm it is well-formed and that `known_anomalies:` and `known_shape_anomalies:` are both present as distinct top-level keys with 3 records each.
  - Confirm `git diff --numstat` shows ZERO changes to docs/status/requirement_status.yaml.
  - Confirm the index's `volumes:` entry for docs/status/requirement_status.yaml still reads `status: closed` WITH the digest -- this is what makes the three new records legal under A4b's closed-and-pinned rule, and the gate verified it on disk at index lines 34/46. If that ever changed, every record would fail.
  - Run `mix letflow.check` and quote the real result. The suite is expected RED for the pre-existing ISS-0109/ISS-0116 tenant-schema class; REVIEWER established at Step 3d that this branch adds no failure main lacks, BUT that proof EXPIRED when Step 4 added .exs files, so do not restate it. Report what you observe and attribute only what you can evidence. TEST-RUNNER re-establishes the baseline at Step 4c.

Note the invariant test currently on the branch still implements the PRE-amendment A4, so it is expected to be RED on the three shape anomalies until TEST-DESIGNER applies §13.5. That is expected, not a regression you caused -- say so plainly rather than treating it as your failure or as success.

handoffs/orchestrator.log has uncommitted ORCH edits and docs/issues/ISS-0193.yaml is a new untracked ORCH file -- leave BOTH alone, do not commit them. Stage by explicit path, never `git add -A`.
acceptance_criteria: §13.4's verbatim block is appended to docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml at the specified insertion point, comment header included
§13.8's verbatim addendum is inserted into docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml's header at the ENTRY SHAPE anchor
The three on-disk entries were re-read and each §13.4 record confirmed to match by line, req, event and field detail, with the read quoted
The edited index parses under a real YAML parser, with known_anomalies: and known_shape_anomalies: both present as distinct top-level keys carrying 3 records each
git diff --numstat confirms ZERO changes to docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, and frozen_prefix_sha256 is unchanged
The index's volumes: entry for volume 1 is confirmed still status: closed with its digest, which is what makes the new records legal under A4b

No test file, design artefact, existing known_anomalies record or A5 text was modified

result.summary:
Applied §13's two gated edits verbatim; wrote zero bytes into volume 1.

EDIT 1 — index. §13.4's 75-line block appended verbatim to docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml at top level (column 0) immediately after the existing known_anomalies: block, which was the end of the file; it now occupies index lines 91-165. The comment header is included in full, including the 'A RECORD MAY ONLY CITE A CLOSED, DIGEST-PINNED VOLUME' paragraph and the kind: vocabulary paragraph. Nothing above it changed.

EDIT 2 — volume-2 header. §13.8's nine comment lines inserted verbatim into docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml's header immediately after the '── ENTRY SHAPE — all five fields, in this order, every time ──' block (v2:60-67), now occupying v2:68-76, ahead of the '── `req:` — THE COMPLETE LIST' heading. No existing header line was changed, so A8 clauses (a) and (b) are unaffected, and clause (c)'s literal token known_shape_anomalies: is present at v2:72.

Both blocks were extracted programmatically from the artefact's fenced code blocks (md lines 1200-1274 and 1398-1406) and written byte-for-byte rather than retyped, so transcription drift is not possible. Both target files are LF-terminated and stayed LF.

ONE BYTE-LEVEL DEVIATION, DISCLOSED. I added a single '#' separator comment line after the §13.8 addendum (v2:77) so the addendum does not abut the next '── `req:`' heading, matching the header's own comment-separator convention on every other section boundary. It is a blank comment line carrying no content, and it is the only line in either edit not lifted verbatim from the artefact. That is why v2's diff is +10 rather than +9. Flagging it rather than leaving it to be discovered.

RE-READ OF THE THREE ON-DISK ENTRIES (docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, unmodified working tree, line numbers from awk NR). All three §13.4 records match by line, req, event and field detail:
  4803|  - req: REQ-053 / 4804|    event: started / 4805|    agent: ORCH / 4806|    at: "2026-08-19T02:35:30Z" / 4807|(blank)  -> four fields, no note:. Matches record 1 (entry_line 4803, REQ-053, started, missing_field, field note, found_as/found_line null).
  4896|  - req: REQ-056 / 4897|    event: started / 4898|    agent: ORCH / 4899|    timestamp: "2026-08-19T02:40:35Z" / 4900|    note: >  -> five fields, but the timestamp field is named timestamp:, at line 4899 exactly. Matches record 2 (entry_line 4896, REQ-056, started, misnamed_field, field at, found_as timestamp, found_line 4899), including should_have_been 'at: "2026-08-19T02:40:35Z"' — the value on disk is character-identical.
  5050|  - req: REQ-054 / 5051|    event: started / 5052|    agent: ORCH / 5053|    at: "2026-08-19T03:50:35Z" / 5054|(blank)  -> four fields, no note:. Matches record 3 (entry_line 5050, REQ-054, started, missing_field, field note, found_as/found_line null).
No disagreement with the gate in any particular, so the stop-and-report condition was not triggered. Corroborated by anchored field arithmetic over volume 1: '^  - req: ' 182, '^    event: ' 182, '^    agent: ' 182, '^    at: ' 181, '^    note: ' 180, and '^    timestamp: ' matching exactly once, at 4899 — one missing at:, two missing note:, nothing else.

YAML PARSE OF THE EDITED INDEX (PyYAML safe_load): well-formed. Top-level keys ['roll_rule', 'volumes', 'known_anomalies', 'known_shape_anomalies'] — both anomaly keys present as DISTINCT top-level keys, 3 records each. The three known_shape_anomalies records load as {4803, REQ-053, started, missing_field, note, None, None}, {4896, REQ-056, started, misnamed_field, at, timestamp, 4899}, {5050, REQ-054, started, missing_field, note, None, None}. docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml also still parses (keys ['history']).

VOLUME 1 UNTOUCHED. Full-tree `git diff --numstat`: 76/0 docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml, 10/0 docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml, 11/0 handoffs/orchestrator.log (ORCH's, not mine, not staged). docs/status/requirement_status.yaml does NOT appear at all — zero changes, zero insertions, zero deletions. frozen_prefix_sha256 in the index is unchanged at 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804, and I recomputed it independently over volume 1's lines 1-5766 with CRLF normalised to LF and every line terminated by a single \n: 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804. Match. (My first attempt printed bb52be74da4a750b097edcdbfc0d4d10c56cda65fa1dab34732c922ff7eea54e — that was a bug in my own throwaway script, which read with newline='' and re-joined without stripping the \r, i.e. it hashed a stream that was never the defined one. Corrected, it matches. Recording it so the wrong digest is not later mistaken for evidence of anything.) frozen_prefix_lines 5766, entries 182, lines 5766, bytes_working_tree 361376, roll_rule and all three existing known_anomalies records are byte-identical — the index diff is purely additive at end-of-file.

A4b LEGALITY PRECONDITION CONFIRMED ON DISK: the index's volumes: entry for docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (index lines 32-52) still reads status: closed (line 34) AND carries frozen_prefix_sha256: (line 46). All three new records cite that path, so all three satisfy A4b's closed-and-pinned rule. Volume 2 is status: current with no digest and is cited by no record.

SUITE. `mix letflow.check` run to completion. Real result, quoted: 'Result: 1271/1284 passed (5/5 properties, 1266/1279 tests)', 'Failed: 13 tests', 'Finished in 556.3 seconds (6.3s async, 549.9s sync)', task exit '** (Mix) mix letflow.check.test: FAILED -- underlying `mix test` run exited 2 (real test failure/error).' Enumerated with `mix test --failed`, which reproduced all 13 (0/13 passed): 9 in Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest (REQ-063 §4 copy_tenant/copy_all_tenants, REQ-063 §5 drop-guard idempotency/skip-on-uncopied-row, ISS-0060 self-heal and with_only_this_tenant_visible!/2) — the pre-existing tenant-schema class; 2 in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest (its own meta-tests over check.test's ISS-0069 warning detection); 1 is A4 in test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs. None of the 12 non-A4 failures live in a file this change touches, and this change adds no code — but I am deliberately NOT restating REVIEWER's Step 3d proof that this branch adds no failure main lacks, since it expired when Step 4 added .exs files. I did not re-derive a main baseline myself; TEST-RUNNER re-establishes it at Step 4c. Attribution beyond what is written above is not evidenced by me.

A4 IS RED, AND THAT IS EXPECTED — neither my failure nor a success. The invariant test on this branch still implements the PRE-amendment A4, which has no shape-exception mechanism; its own failure text says so: 'The index has NO declaration mechanism for shape violations — see the note in test/specs/ISS-0119.md.' Run alone the file is 9/10, and A4's message names exactly the three anomalies this amendment declares and nothing else: 'shape violations (3): %{line: 4803, path: "docs/status/requirement_status.yaml", req: "REQ-053", problem: {:field_set_or_order, [:req, :event, :agent, :at]}}', '%{line: 4896, ..., req: "REQ-056", problem: {:field_set_or_order, [:req, :event, :agent, :timestamp, :note]}}', '%{line: 5050, ..., req: "REQ-054", problem: {:field_set_or_order, [:req, :event, :agent, :at]}}', with 'undeclared vocabulary violations (0): (none)'. That is a third independent confirmation — from the detector itself — that the declared set equals the on-disk set exactly, and that A5's vocabulary set is arithmetically unaffected. A4 goes green only once TEST-DESIGNER applies §13.5's A4a/A4b split, which is the next step. Nothing here should be read as A4b having passed: A4b does not exist yet.

NOT TOUCHED: docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (zero bytes), lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md, every file under test/, the three existing known_anomalies records, and A5's text. handoffs/orchestrator.log (modified by ORCH) and docs/issues/ISS-0193.yaml (new untracked ORCH file) were left alone and are absent from the commit — staging was by explicit path, never `git add -A`.

It is the only line in either edit not verbatim from the artefact, carries no content, and does not affect A8 clause (c) — the literal token known_shape_anomalies: is present at v2:72. Per §13.10 it must NOT be cleared by editing the declared list or narrowing the detector.

BASELINE NOT ESTABLISHED BY ME: 12 further failures observed (9 Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest, 2 Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest). REVIEWER's Step 3d no-added-failure proof expired when Step 4 added .exs files, and I did not re-derive a main baseline. TEST-RUNNER re-establishes it at Step 4c.
